clue.text: Able to pay back Fanny Adams for 500 buckles

indicators.note: something that buckles bends out of shape, so the two initials are twisted round

parts.note: Fanny Adams, as in 'sweet FA', is abbreviated to its initials
taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Someone can repay sweet nothing, and the fee of five hundred falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' belongs to the definition rather than signalling a reversal; 'buckles' turns FA into AF, then FOR as written and the Roman D follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford something is to have the means to pay for it, so being able to pay fits the verb loosely.

clue.text: According to prescription, cast's top class and non-clerical

parts.note: a cast is a mould or shape, which is a form
U stands for upper class, the top class
laic means of the laity, not clergy

explanation.surface: A theatre cast's leading figure is upper-class and secular, as if prescribed.
explanation.definitionFit: Formulaic means following a set formula, as a prescription lays down exactly what to do.

clue.text: Prayer for gold is working!

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
taken as written
a machine that is working is switched on

explanation.surface: An exclamation that praying for gold is paying off.
explanation.definitionFit: An orison is an old literary word for a prayer.

clue.text: Canine's canine found by Violet

parts.note: a canine is a dog, so canine's is dog's
a canine is also a pointed tooth

explanation.surface: A dog's fang turns up beside a girl called Violet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' is used in its two senses, the animal and the tooth; 'found by' only joins them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog's-tooth violet is a spring flowering plant, Erythronium, named for its pointed bulb.

clue.text: Be around in frilly collar for cold shoulder

indicators.note: in puts the turned letters inside the collar

parts.note: a ruff is a frilled Elizabethan collar

indicators.note: around turns the word be backwards

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a frilly ruff is snubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuff someone is to snub them, which is giving them the cold shoulder.

clue.text: Pixie (Irish) brought up in Winchester?

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from the bottom upwards, so both pieces are turned

parts.note: a pixie is an elf

explanation.surface: An Irish fairy raised in the English cathedral city of Winchester.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchester looks like the Hampshire city; the question mark marks it as an example, the Winchester rifle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winchester is a famous make of repeating firearm, an example of the weapon.

clue.text: Bono in hospital? On the contrary, with expression almost of exuberant friendliness

indicators.note: in, read the other way round, puts one piece inside the other
on the contrary reverses which piece contains which, so the hospital goes inside the singer

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a mien is a facial expression or bearing

explanation.surface: The rock singer Bono, laid up in hospital, wears a cheerful face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips the container: the hospital goes inside the singer, not the singer inside the hospital. 'almost' drops the final letter of the expression word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonhomie is cheerful good nature, a warm and exuberant friendliness.

clue.text: River's direction can be deceptive

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
SE, south-east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: The way a river flows can mislead.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: False means untrue or misleading, which is what deceptive means.

clue.text: Albert leaves opera to fish

indicators.note: leaves means the name goes away from the title

parts.note: Albert Herring is a comic opera by Benjamin Britten
taken as written

explanation.surface: Albert walks out of the opera house to go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Herring is Britten's 1947 comic opera; take the hero's first name out of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: The herring is a common silvery sea fish of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: My Pat and Esther are volatile, having a tendency to fly off the handle

definitions.text: a tendency to fly off the handle

indicators.note: volatile means unstable and liable to change, so these letters rearrange

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pat and Esther both lose their tempers easily.
explanation.definitionFit: A hasty temper is a quick, short fuse, an inclination to lose one's temper suddenly.

clue.text: Buff card allocated to followers

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or fan
a club is a playing card of the black suit with the trefoil

explanation.surface: A pale yellow card is handed out to supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan club is an organised body of devotees who follow a star or team.

clue.text: Wartime fashion?

parts.note: reads as clothing styles of a war era, but means the uniform soldiers wear for fighting

explanation.definitionFit: Battledress is the everyday combat uniform of soldiers, literally the dress worn in war.

clue.text: Instant incentive? Don't even think about it!

definitions.meaning: a goad that exists only for an instant, a spur belonging to the present moment
the cry of someone acting on impulse, with no forethought at all

explanation.definitionFit: Spur-of-the-moment describes an impulsive act done without planning or reflection.

clue.text: Old solvers with a right to some time

parts.note: ye is the old plural form of you, the solvers addressed by the clue

explanation.surface: Veteran puzzlers claim a right to a bit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a fixed stretch of time, twelve months long.

clue.text: Very old pet comes to island with lake by calling

parts.note: a cat is a household pet
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: An elderly pet arrives on an island beside a loch.
explanation.definitionFit: Vocational means relating to a vocation, so a job held by calling is vocational.

clue.text: Tottering in boat, Mae can't stand

indicators.note: tottering means unsteady and wobbling, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wobbling in a boat, Mae cannot keep her feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't stand' looks like losing balance in the boat; it is the definition, meaning loathe.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate something is to loathe it, to be unable to stand it.

clue.text: Chap following poor Nigel is forgetful

indicators.note: following puts the chap after the scrambled name
poor means badly made, so the name is rearranged

parts.note: a gent is a chap, a man

explanation.surface: A man trails after unfortunate Nigel, who keeps forgetting things.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent means careless or neglectful, failing to remember duties, so forgetful.

clue.text: Malicious gossip gets around, conveyed without being loud

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the sent letters surround the rest

parts.note: conveyed means sent

indicators.note: gets around means the gossip word is turned backwards

parts.note: dirt is scandalous or malicious gossip

explanation.surface: Spiteful rumour spreads, carried along quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without being loud' reads as quiet; 'without' is the outside container signal and 'loud' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means harsh and loud, grating on the ear.

clue.text: Shield sniffer retreating round wounded companion with drug

indicators.note: round means the turned sniffer goes around the other pieces
retreating means going backwards, so the word for sniffer is reversed

parts.note: a sniffer is a nose
wounded means cut
CH stands for Companion of Honour
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A sniffer dog backs away from an injured friend carrying drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: An escutcheon is the shield on which a coat of arms is displayed.

clue.text: Having got on, agreed about having been left out

indicators.note: having been left out means these letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone who boarded agreed, though annoyed at being excluded.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has got on in years is old, so aged.

clue.text: Time of the openings of royal homes you thoughtfully had mentioned

indicators.note: the openings of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Remembering a visit to the royal palaces you once mused about.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, rhythm is the pattern of beats, also called time.

clue.text: Why fat girl I pine about is potentially dangerous

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned about into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man wonders why he longs for a plump girl, a risky business.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing with fire is an idiom for taking a dangerous risk.

clue.text: Gascoigne losing his head is a caution

indicators.note: losing his head means the first letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Bamber Gascoigne was the long-serving host of the quiz show University Challenge

explanation.surface: A footballer, losing his temper, is a real character.
explanation.walkthrough: Gascoigne suggests the footballer Paul Gascoigne; it is Bamber Gascoigne, British TV quiz host.
explanation.definitionFit: An amber traffic light warns drivers to take caution before stopping.

clue.text: Man across the way is windy

indicators.note: across means the man's letters stretch over the way

parts.note: a guy is a man
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A man on the other side of the road is blustery.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusty weather is marked by sudden blasts of wind, so windy.

clue.text: Masseurs get overshoes in New York

definitions.meaning: people who give massages rub people down
in American English, rubber galoshes worn over shoes

explanation.definitionFit: Rubbers are both people who rub and, in US English, waterproof overshoes.

clue.text: From the start, lessons will be simple

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Lessons from the first day are going to be easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means without guile or sophistication, natural and simple.

clue.text: Small-minded about redhead being attractive

indicators.note: about means the petty letters go around the other one

parts.note: petty means small-minded
the head of the word red is R

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded view of a redhead's looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty is a synonym for attractive, pleasing to look at.

clue.text: Neighbours playing with German youth initially may display ill will

parts.note: in bridge East and North are neighbouring players at the table
mit is German for with

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word youth

explanation.surface: Children at play next door with a young German can turn hostile.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is hostility or hatred, the state of bearing ill will.
